transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Ethan Parker (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood Legal Ops); Rachel Chen (Pinnacle Procurement), Derek Lowe (Legal), Marco Ruiz (Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Security), Tommy Ng (Finops)

Summary:
Quick procurement + legal alignment on pilot terms, SLA thresholds, and implementation window. Customer wants a 30-day pilot, scoped to two APIs (chat + embeddings), with committed spend options and an ask for VPC/private routing for PHI workloads. Several MSA/DPA redlines flagged; need SOC 2 / audit evidence and clarity on KMS options. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and duration
- Pricing structure (committed vs pay-as-you-go)
- SLA windows, uptime and latency targets for chat endpoints
- DPA/MSA redlines and data residency / PHI handling
- KMS and encryption (bring-your-own-key options)
- Implementation window / go-live timeline and rollback conditions

Action items (also captured in metadata):
- Samira to run 48-hour latency/cost benchmarks across sample prompts
- Ethan to share commercial worksheet and pilot pricing options
- Priya to suggest MSA redline concessions and DPA notes
- Sofia to provide details on which services will carry PHI and needed residency

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Ethan Parker: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. We're, uh, Ethan from Redwood, AE. Quick round robin?
[00:00:10] Rachel Chen: Rachel here, procurement at Pinnacle, thanks. We've got legal and platform on too.
[00:00:14] Derek Lowe: Derek, counsel. We'll be focused on the MSA/DPA points.
[00:00:18] Marco Ruiz: Marco, platform engineer. I'll ask the deep infra questions.
[00:00:22] Samira Khan: Samira, SE at Redwood, I'll do the bench and technical scope.
[00:00:28] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, security. Mainly interested in SOC2 evidence, KMS, and data flows.
[00:00:32] Tommy Ng: Tommy, FinOps. Pricing delta and committed vs burst model.

[00:01:05] Ethan Parker: Cool. The goal today is to align on the pilot: 30 days, two endpoints — chat and embeddings — and confirm we can meet your SLOs and your legal asks. Also to surface any non-starters in the MSA/DPA.
[00:01:18] Derek Lowe: Non-starters: anything that prevents us from controlling data residency or prevents customer-managed keys. We also want explicit obligations for breach notifications — 72 hours is required by our policy.
[00:01:31] Priya Patel: To add, we usually look for indemnity carve-outs around customer data. We'll put specific redlines in — but high level, yes, KMS and residency are big.

[00:02:10] Samira Khan: On the infra side, we support hosted and dedicated. For PHI-heavy workloads we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem options) and you can bring your own key via KMS/HSM integrations. There are nuances: host vs dedicated affects cold start and latency, and quantization options affect cost.
[00:02:30] Marco Ruiz: Clarify quick — if we do private, do you manage the control plane or do we self-host everything?
[00:02:36] Luis Ortega: (interjecting) We provide a private control plane with customer-managed networking; for on-prem it's customer-run nodes with Redwood orchestration. Sorry that was a mouthful.
[00:02:46] Marco Ruiz: Okay that's helpful.

[00:03:15] Rachel Chen: On pricing — Tommy wants committed spend options. We need an estimate for the 30-day pilot and a proposal for convert-to-paid terms.
[00:03:22] Tommy Ng: Right, and also what happens if we exceed committed tokens — buffer/burst pricing and auto-billing limits.
[00:03:29] Ethan Parker: We'll put options: small commit, mid commit, and pay-as-you-go with burst caps. We'll include an overage rate and an opt-in for burst capacity.

[00:04:00] Derek Lowe: On the MSA redlines — we'll send a markup but two quick asks: 1) no broad data-license grant for customer data, and 2) liability cap alignment with our procurement policy (we may need to carve exceptions).
[00:04:12] Priya Patel: Noted. From Redwood legal, we are usually flexible on data licensing — we can explicitly state no ownership transfer — and liability caps we can discuss based on commitment levels.

[00:05:05] Samira Khan: Technical question from Marco — latency SLOs: for chat with sequence lengths under 512 tokens we target p95 under 300ms on dedicated; hosted is higher variance, p95 around 600-800ms depending on load. The embeddings endpoint is much cheaper and usually sub-100ms p95 on dedicated.
[00:05:28] Marco Ruiz: 300ms p95 is good. Is that measured from our client to response or just service-side?
[00:05:33] Samira Khan: Service-side. Client-to-response will add network egress, but if we colocate in your VPC region it's usually additional 30-80ms.

[00:06:10] Sofia Alvarez: Bandwidth and egress costs are a concern. Do you have egress pricing separate? For healthcare data, cross-region transfers are restricted.
[00:06:18] Ethan Parker: Yes, egress fees apply only if data leaves the region or we need to move logs out. For Private deployments inside the same region, egress is minimal. We'll include a matrix in the pricing doc.

[00:07:00] Marco Ruiz: Data residency — we need to ensure PHI never leaves US-East region for the pilot. Can you pin nodes to a region?
[00:07:07] Luis Ortega: Yes, we can pin routing by policy. We'll route by region and customer tier; fallback policies exist but can be disabled for strict residency. Sometimes the transcription mislabels that as "route policy pinning" but yes it's region pinning.

[00:07:40] Derek Lowe: DPA specifics: we need subprocessors list, standard contractual clauses if we move data internationally, and encryption at rest with customer keys.
[00:07:49] Priya Patel: Subprocessors list is a living doc; we'll provide current list and commit to notice of changes. For encryption, we support BYOK via KMS; HSM integration is available for Dedicated/Private.

[00:09:10] Tommy Ng: About pilot metrics: we'll want tokens consumed, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens breakdown daily. Can you surface per-route billing?
[00:09:19] Samira Khan: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route and per-model token breakdown, plus tracing hooks. We'll share a sample console export.

[00:10:05] Rachel Chen: Implementation window — we can't have production traffic until legal signs. Our target is pilot start 2026-12-07 and finish 2027-01-06, with a go/no-go at day 21. Any issues with that timeline?
[00:10:18] Ethan Parker: Timeline seems doable. Two weeks for onboarding and infra; we can compress if we pre-share network details. We'll commit to a playbook for rollback and a 48-hour hotfix SLA during the pilot.

[00:11:00] Marco Ruiz: Network prep details — we'll need firewall rules, allowed IPs, and SSH cert details if using private nodes.
[00:11:08] Luis Ortega: We'll send a network checklist. Note: some customers use private peering, others use TLS endpoints in VPC — both supported.

[00:12:30] Derek Lowe: Let's talk about indemnity and data breach timelines again — 72 hours is our minimum. Also, we want to ensure logs retention is configurable and we can request exports for audits.
[00:12:40] Priya Patel: We can commit to 72-hour notification and provide audit logs; retention settings can be set at customer level with retention export. I'll put the specifics in the DPA redline doc.

[00:13:50] Sofia Alvarez: For SOC2: do you have the report and do you allow customers to view the evidence?
[00:13:56] Priya Patel: We can provide the SOC2 type II report and a control matrix. Evidence access is on request; for high-sensitivity customers we can walk through the report with our security team.

[00:15:05] Marco Ruiz: Back to SLAs — what's the financial credit model? Is it credits per minute of downtime or percentage of monthly uptime?
[00:15:12] Samira Khan: Typically monthly uptime percentage with a tiered credit schedule: e.g., <99.9% credit X, <99.5% credit Y. For latency breaches (p95 above SLA) we provide non-monetary remedies or credits depending on the contract level. We can discuss stronger remedies for Dedicated.

[00:16:00] Tommy Ng: We might need a higher SLA for the core API during business hours. Can we have an elevated SLO for 9am-5pm EST with stronger credits?
[00:16:09] Ethan Parker: Yes, we can create time-of-day windows for stronger SLOs at a premium. That would typically be part of Dedicated or an add-on.

[00:17:30] Rachel Chen: For procurement, we'll want a clean commercial term sheet with: pilot fees, committed rate, overage rate, and conversion pricing with discount tiers.
[00:17:38] Ethan Parker: We'll draft three options and show historical cost curves from similar customers (anonymized).

[00:18:50] Derek Lowe: One more legal point: we may ask for certain subcontractor privacy audits. Do you accept customer audits or do you provide third-party attestations?
[00:19:00] Priya Patel: We generally provide third-party attestations (SOC2, ISO when available) and a subprocessors list; direct customer audits are rare but negotiable under enterprise agreements.

[00:20:30] Marco Ruiz: Technical deep dive request: can you run a 48-hour benchmark with our prompt set to measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost? We'll want the raw trace.
[00:20:40] Samira Khan: Yes, we'll run that. Send us a sample corpus and we'll drop the results into a shared sheet. There might be some mis-transcriptions here; I meant a "sample corpus" not "campus".

[00:21:50] Sofia Alvarez: For KMS: do you support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault? We use AWS KMS for most keys.
[00:21:57] Luis Ortega: We integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault and customers can bring HSM-backed keys on Dedicated. There are a few setup steps for key rotation.

[00:23:10] Tommy Ng: Cost modeling question — if we enable prefix caching and batching, what's the typical cost reduction?
[00:23:19] Samira Khan: Batching and KV/prefix caching can drop token cost by 20-40% depending on prompt reuse. We'll include recommended batching configs in the Optimize report.

[00:24:30] Derek Lowe: Any export control concerns? We won't be sending certain PII internationally. We need assurance egress controls are in the DPA.
[00:24:38] Priya Patel: We'll include egress controls and data handling sections in the DPA. If necessary, we can restrict crossing borders for the pilot.

[00:26:00] Ethan Parker: Let's go rapid-fire on open items and owners so we have clarity.
[00:26:05] Rachel Chen: Procurement needs pilot pricing and conversion terms — owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-11-30.
[00:26:12] Tommy Ng: FinOps wants the per-route cost breakdown and an overage cap — owner: Samira. Due: 2026-12-03.
[00:26:20] Derek Lowe: Legal will provide redlines and a prioritized list of non-negotiables — owner: Derek. Due: 2026-11-29.
[00:26:26] Priya Patel: Redwood legal will respond to the redlines and propose compromise language — owner: Priya. Due: 2026-11-30.

[00:28:00] Samira Khan: We'll need your sample prompts and a CSV of traffic patterns. That will let us reproduce latencies with the bench harness.
[00:28:08] Marco Ruiz: We'll share sample prompts and expected concurrency window.

[00:30:00] (cut: background noise, unrelated small talk)

[00:31:00] Ethan Parker: One last commercial nuance — if you choose Dedicated vs Hosted at conversion, the ramp and termination clauses differ. We'll show a transition plan in the worksheet.
[00:31:10] Rachel Chen: Good. Also, are there early termination fees for the pilot if we stop after day 10?
[00:31:16] Ethan Parker: Pilot termination is typically low friction — small administrative fee only. We'll include the exact language.

[00:32:30] Sofia Alvarez: Security-specific: can you turn off model telemetry for the PHI path? We want logs but scrubbed PII.
[00:32:38] Luis Ortega: Yes, we have controls for telemetry and PII scrubbing; we also support log redaction and granular log retention.

[00:34:00] Marco Ruiz: Will you provide an SLA for database KV cache availability? Some of our workflows rely on persistent KV.
[00:34:08] Samira Khan: KV cache has its own availability profile; for Dedicated we give stronger durability SLAs. We'll include that in the technical appendix.

[00:36:20] Derek Lowe: A question on indemnity again: if there's a data breach caused by your subprocessors, what's the liability path?
[00:36:27] Priya Patel: We'll propose language where Redwood remains responsible for its subprocessors' compliance; specific carve-outs and caps can be negotiated in the main agreement.

[00:38:00] Tommy Ng: A quick competitor question — are there features your platform has that Anthropic or OpenAI don't offer for enterprise-grade deployments?
[00:38:07] Ethan Parker: We highlight unified inference across hosted/dedicated/private, per-route billing, and routing policies plus first-class rollout and fallback. Also strong ops visibility in Redwood Console.

[00:40:20] Rachel Chen: Ok let's recap and confirm next steps verbally.
[00:40:25] Ethan Parker: Recap: Redwood to send commercial worksheet + pilot pricing (Ethan) by 2026-11-30; SE to run 48-hour bench and share sheet (Samira) by 2026-12-03; Redwood legal to produce MSA/DPA redline guidance (Priya) by 2026-11-30; Pinnacle legal to send markup (Derek) by 2026-11-29; Customer to share sample prompts and data residency list (Sofia/Marco) by 2026-11-29; Schedule SOC2 evidence workshop (owner: Priya/Sofia) tentatively 2026-12-08. Any objections?
[00:41:00] Derek Lowe: No objections.
[00:41:05] Rachel Chen: Sounds good.

[00:42:00] (small side conversation about holiday coverage, unclear transcription)

[00:50:00] Ethan Parker: Thanks all, we'll follow up with meeting notes and a short checklist. Expect the redline-friendly MSA summary and the pricing worksheet in the next business day or two.
[00:50:10] Rachel Chen: Thanks. Appreciate it.
[00:50:15] Marco Ruiz: Bye.

[00:50:30] (call ends)

Closing notes: action owners and deadlines repeated in email thread; seed documents to be shared: pilot pricing worksheet, network checklist, DPA redline guide, benchmark spreadsheet.
